q: You lean on the starboard guardrail by the gate and find this. What do you do?
answer: Ask the base to fix all three before you leave — the guardrail is what keeps the crew aboard
why: A loose stanchion or a frayed lifeline fails when someone falls on it; the base fixes it, not the form.

q: At the cabin-top winches you run each halyard and clutch. What do you do before you sign?
answer: The clutch freed and the third handle found now; the chafe and the jaws on the form
why: A clutch that will not release is a halyard you cannot drop; a missing handle is a deposit charge on Friday.

figure.note: Clutch #2 jammed shut · 2 of 3 winch handles found

ru.Clutch #2 jammed shut · 2 of 3 winch han: Стопор №2 заклинил · найдено 2 из 3 ручек лебёдки

q: You load the starboard primary winch with the genoa sheet and feel this. What do you do?
answer: Ask the base to service the winch now — a slipping pawl lets the sheet run back
why: Pawls stop the drum turning back; worn or stuck, they let the sheet run out under load and take a hand with it.

q: The genoa is fully unrolled. You look at the furling drum and see this. What do you ask for?
answer: The line rewound tight on the drum with the sail fully out
why: With the sail fully out the drum must hold enough line to roll it all in; one turn left means the line runs out mid-furl.

figure.note: Genoa fully out · rest of the line slack on deck

ru.Genoa fully out · rest of the line slack: Генуя полностью раскрыта · остаток линя лежит на палубе

q: The technician runs the genoa sheet through the car for you. You check the car itself and see this. What do you ask for?
answer: The plunger pin replaced so the car locks in the track
why: A car that is not pinned slides under load: the sheet lead goes and the car can hit the end stop; the pin is a base fix.

figure.note: Starboard car lashed to the track with cord · port car OK

ru.Starboard car lashed to the track with c: Правая каретка привязана к погону шнурком · левая в порядке

q: You run the genoa sheets to the winches and look at them. What do you ask for?
answer: The port sheet replaced and the second spare line found before you sign
why: A bare core fails under load and a 14 m sheet will not reach the winch on a wide genoa; spares are counted, not assumed.

figure.note: Port 14 m · starboard 16 m · spare lines: list 2, found 1

ru.Port 14 m · starboard 16 m · spare lines: Левый 14 м · правый 16 м · запасные концы: по списку 2, найден 1

q: The boat has in-mast furling. The technician asks you to unfurl the main yourself. How do you do it?
answer: Outhaul out on the winch, the furling line eased with a little tension kept on
why: The roll must stay firm as it leaves the mast: slack on the furling line lets it bunch and jam in the slot; never winch against a closed clutch.

figure.note: In-mast main · outhaul on the winch, furling line in a clutch

ru.In-mast main · outhaul on the winch, fur: Грот в мачте · аутхол на лебёдке, линь закрутки в стопоре

q: You follow the genoa furling line from the drum aft along the side deck and find this. What do you ask for?
answer: A lead block fitted at the gap so the line runs fair, not over the stanchion base
why: A furling line chafing on a stanchion base jams or parts mid-furl; the lead blocks are the base's fittings, counted like the rest.

figure.note: Furling line, drum to cockpit · list: 4 blocks, fitted: 3

ru.Furling line, drum to cockpit · list: 4: Линь закрутки, от барабана в кокпит · по списку 4 блока, стоят 3

q: On the hoist the technician stops winching at this point. Your crew ask what the tape is for. What do you tell them?
answer: It marks full hoist: stop there, or the headboard jams against the masthead sheave
why: A halyard winched past its mark drives the headboard into the sheave: the halyard stretches, the sail will not come down.

figure.note: Main at full hoist · black tape 5 cm short of the clutch

ru.Main at full hoist · black tape 5 cm sho: Грот поднят полностью · чёрная изолента в 5 см от стопора

q: The main halyard goes to an electric winch. The technician shows you the button. What rule do you give the crew?
answer: Short pushes, eyes on the sail, stop at any snag — never hold the button against a load
why: An electric winch does not feel a snag: a batten in a lazyjack or a jammed slide tears before the motor notices.

figure.note: Push-button at the coachroof · two speeds · halyard 10 mm

ru.Push-button at the coachroof · two speed: Кнопка на рубке · две скорости · фал 10 мм

q: Hoisting the main at the pontoon, your crew member on the winch feels it stop and asks whether to keep winching. You look up and see this. What do you say?
answer: Stop — ease a little so the batten drops clear of the lazyjack, then hoist again by hand
why: A batten end winched against a lazyjack tears the pocket; slack the lazyjacks forward or head to wind, and hoist with eyes aloft.

figure.note: Hoist stops at two-thirds · lazyjack across the batten pocket

ru.Hoist stops at two-thirds · lazyjack acr: Подъём встал на двух третях · лейзи-джек поперёк кармана латы

q: Main sheeted in at the pontoon, you load the mainsheet by hand and the tail creeps through the cleat. What do you ask for?
answer: The cam cleat replaced before you sign — a mainsheet that will not hold cannot be trusted on a gybe
why: The mainsheet must hold on its own cleat under full load; worn cam teeth let the boom out in a gust, with crew in the way.

figure.note: Sheet loaded by hand · tail creeps 10 cm, then holds

ru.Sheet loaded by hand · tail creeps 10 cm: Нагрузка рукой · хвост ползёт 10 см, потом держит

q: The technician makes a stern line up on the midships cleat to show you the cleat hitch. The line looks like this. What do you do?
answer: Ask for it replaced before departure and note the swap on the form
why: A chafed, hardened line parts in the first Meltemi night; mooring lines are the base's to replace, not yours.

figure.note: Hard, kinked; cover worn through in one place

ru.Hard, kinked; cover worn through in one: Жёсткий, в заломах; оплётка протёрта в одном месте

q: At the quay demonstration the technician hauls the lazy line up bare-handed. You will also pick up buoys in the bays. What do you check is aboard before you sign?
answer: Gloves for the slime line and a boat hook that locks when extended
why: Lazy lines are slimy and cut hands; the boat hook that does the buoys and lines must lock, not telescope back.

figure.note: Slime line hauled up by hand

q: Your crew ask how to tie the fenders on before the first quay. What do you show them?
answer: A clove hitch with a slipped half hitch, so the height changes fast
why: A clove hitch is re-set in seconds for a quay or a pontoon; the slipped half hitch stops it shaking loose.

figure.note: Height set for the quay, then made fast

q: Thursday night, stern-to at a town quay with a swell running in. The stern lines are creaking and you see this. What do you do?
answer: Fit chafe guards at the fairlead and the quay edge, and ease the line a little
why: Chafe, not strain, parts mooring lines; a sleeve or a length of hose where the line moves keeps it whole till morning.

figure.note: Line sawing on the fairlead and the quay edge

ru.Line sawing on the fairlead and the quay: Конец пилит клюз и кромку причала

q: Wednesday evening, stern-to at a quay. You plan to leave at 06:00, when nobody will be ashore. How do you get the stern lines back aboard?
answer: Just before leaving, double each one back through its ring and slip it from aboard
why: A line doubled through the ring is let go from the boat: nobody jumps a widening gap, and nothing is left on the quay.

figure.note: Leaving at 06:00, nobody on the quay
